Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) -- Michael Jackson knew "exactly how his fate would be played out" and feared his death would echo that of Elvis Presley, Lisa Marie Presley wrote in an online blog posted Friday morning. Michael Jackson and Lisa Marie Presley in 1994. Presley says, "I loved him very much" and believes he loved her. Presley -- the daughter of Elvis, the "King of Rock," and the ex-wife of Jackson, the "King of Pop" -- wrote on her MySpace page that she wanted "to say now what I have never said before because I want the truth out there for once." Her publicist confirmed Presley wrote the blog. She said her short marriage to Jackson -- from May 1994 until January 1996 -- "was not 'a sham' as is being reported in the press," but she divorced him because she was "in over my head in trying" to save Jackson "from the inevitable, which is what has just happened." Jackson talked with her about his death during "a deep conversation" 14 years ago about "the circumstances of my father's death."  Watch more from Presley on Jackson » . "At some point he paused, he stared at me very intensely and he stated with an almost calm certainty, 'I am afraid that I am going to end up like him, the way he did,' " Presley wrote. "I promptly tried to deter him from the idea, at which point he just shrugged his shoulders and nodded almost matter of fact as if to let me know, he knew what he knew and that was kind of that." That conversation haunted Presley as she watched television coverage of Jackson's death Thursday, she said. "I am sitting here watching on the news [as] an ambulance leaves the driveway of his home, the big gates, the crowds outside the gates, the coverage, the crowds outside the hospital, the cause of death and what may have led up to it and the memory of this conversation hit me, as did the unstoppable tears," she wrote. "A predicted ending by him, by loved ones and by me, but what I didn't predict was how much it was going to hurt when it finally happened." Elvis Presley collapsed in the bathroom of his Memphis, Tennessee, mansion -- Graceland -- on August 16, 1977, at the age of 42. While his death was ruled the result of an irregular heartbeat, the autopsy report was sealed amid accusations that abuse of prescription drugs caused the problem. "As I sit here overwhelmed with sadness, reflection and confusion at what was my biggest failure to date, watching on the news almost play by play the exact scenario I saw happen on August 16, 1977, happening again right now with Michael (A sight I never wanted to see again) just as he predicted, I am truly, truly gutted," she wrote. "I wanted to 'save him'," she wrote. "I wanted to save him from the inevitable, which is what has just happened." "The hardest decision I have ever had to make, which was to walk away and let his fate have him, even though I desperately loved him and tried to stop or reverse it somehow," Presley wrote. Their marriage, which some suggested was only to help Jackson's image, was real, she said. "It was an unusual relationship, yes, where two unusual people who did not live or know a 'normal life' found a connection, perhaps with some suspect timing on his part," she wrote. "Nonetheless, I do believe he loved me as much as he could love anyone and I loved him very much." Presley called Jackson "an incredibly dynamic force and power that was not to be underestimated." "When he used it for something good, it was the best and when he used it for something bad, It was really, REALLY bad," she wrote. Presley's blog entry ended with a thank you to those who would read it. "I really needed to say this right now, thanks for listening." Presley's blog can be found online at http://bit.ly/5wR7p .

LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) — In a blog entry published online Friday morning, Lisa Marie Presley said Michael Jackson appeared to understand how his life would end and worried that he would die in circumstances similar to those surrounding Elvis Presley’s death.

Presley, who was photographed with Jackson in 1994, said she had loved him deeply and believed that he loved her as well.

The daughter of Elvis Presley—the “King of Rock”—and former wife of Jackson—the “King of Pop”—explained on her MySpace page that she was speaking publicly about matters she had never previously discussed because she wanted the truth to be known. Her publicist verified that she authored the post.

Presley insisted that her marriage to Jackson, which lasted from May 1994 to January 1996, was genuine and not a publicity arrangement, despite media reports suggesting otherwise. She said she ultimately ended the relationship because her attempts to protect Jackson from what she viewed as an unavoidable outcome had become more than she could handle.

According to Presley, Jackson discussed his own death with her during a serious conversation 14 years earlier about the way her father had died. She recalled that Jackson stopped, looked at her intently and said with quiet conviction that he feared he would meet the same kind of end as Elvis. Presley said she immediately tried to persuade him not to think that way, but Jackson simply shrugged and nodded as though he was certain of what lay ahead.

She said the memory of that exchange returned forcefully while she watched television reports about Jackson’s death on Thursday. News footage showed an ambulance leaving his property, the gates outside his home, crowds gathering there and at the hospital, and speculation about the cause of death and the events preceding it. Presley wrote that the images brought back the conversation and left her crying uncontrollably.

Although Jackson, those close to him and Presley herself had all anticipated such an ending, she said she had not understood how painful it would be when it actually occurred.

Elvis Presley died at age 42 after collapsing in a bathroom at Graceland, his mansion in Memphis, Tennessee, on August 16, 1977. His death was officially attributed to an irregular heartbeat. However, his autopsy report was sealed as allegations circulated that prescription-drug misuse had contributed to the condition.

Presley said she felt overcome by grief, confusion and reflection as she watched the events surrounding Jackson’s death unfold almost moment by moment in a way that reminded her of August 16, 1977. Seeing the same kind of scene repeated with Jackson—just as he had predicted—left her devastated, she wrote.

She described her inability to save him as the greatest failure of her life. Presley said she had desperately wanted to prevent the outcome that had now occurred. Walking away and allowing events to take their course, despite loving him and trying to change his direction, had been the most difficult choice she had ever made.

Addressing claims that their marriage had been intended only to improve Jackson’s public image, Presley again maintained that the relationship was authentic. She acknowledged that it was unconventional: two unusual people, neither of whom had experienced or understood an ordinary life, had formed a bond. She also conceded that Jackson’s timing may have raised doubts. Even so, she believed he loved her as fully as he was capable of loving anyone, and she said she loved him greatly.

Presley characterized Jackson as an exceptionally powerful and dynamic presence whose influence should never have been underestimated. When directed toward something positive, she said, that force could produce extraordinary results; when used negatively, it could be extremely destructive.

She concluded the post by thanking readers, saying she needed to express those thoughts at that moment and appreciated being heard.

Presley’s blog post was available at: http://bit.ly/5wR7p.

# Lisa Marie Presley said Michael Jackson feared he would die like Elvis

**By CNN-style News Desk**

Lisa Marie Presley once recalled that her former husband Michael Jackson believed he would meet a fate similar to that of her father, Elvis Presley.

During a 2010 interview with Oprah Winfrey, Presley said Jackson repeatedly asked about Elvis’ death and expressed concern that his own life would end in much the same way.

“He was always asking me about when he died, how it happened and where,” Presley said. She recalled Jackson telling her, “I’m afraid that I’m going to end up like him, the way he did.”

Elvis Presley died at his Graceland estate in Memphis, Tennessee, in 1977 at age 42. His declining health and use of prescription medication have remained central to accounts of his final years.

Jackson died in 2009 at age 50 after receiving the powerful anesthetic propofol at his Los Angeles home. The Los Angeles County coroner ruled his death a homicide caused by acute propofol intoxication. His physician, Dr. Conrad Murray, was later convicted of involuntary manslaughter.

Lisa Marie Presley, Elvis’ only child, married Jackson in 1994, less than three weeks after finalizing her divorce from musician Danny Keough. The high-profile marriage lasted about two years, though she said the pair continued to have an on-and-off relationship after their divorce.

In the Winfrey interview, Presley described Jackson as intensely focused on the circumstances surrounding Elvis’ death. She also said she had tried to warn Jackson about the people around him and his increasingly troubling behavior, but eventually felt unable to help him.

Presley died in January 2023 at age 54 after suffering complications from a small bowel obstruction. Her posthumous memoir, **“From Here to the Great Unknown,”** was completed by her daughter, actor Riley Keough, and published in 2024, offering additional insight into Presley’s relationships with both her father and Jackson.
